title: The Numbers Keep Jumping

patient.name: Mdm Nur Aisyah
patient.presenting_complaint: Non-contact tonometry giving inconsistent readings across attempts

history.hpc: Mdm Nur says 'Every time the air blow I blink, cannot help it.' The NCT readings vary widely between attempts, partly because she blinks and tears up with each puff.
history.pmhx: No known glaucoma. Watery eyes. No drug allergies.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Watery eyes; otherwise normal by observation
examination_findings.fundus: Not the focus of this station

investigations.task: Recognise unreliable NCT readings, repeat with good technique, and know when to refer for Goldmann applanation tonometry
investigations.key_points: Blinking, tearing and poor fixation cause unreliable NCT; reposition and repeat; if still inconsistent, refer for Goldmann tonometry for an accurate reading rather than recording a doubtful number

diagnosis: The NCT readings are unreliable due to blinking and tearing. The OA recognises the inconsistency, repeats the test with better technique and patient cooperation, and — if still inconsistent — refers for Goldmann applanation tonometry rather than recording a doubtful value. This is a procedural/judgement station.

immediate: Confirm identity and perform hand hygiene; wipe machine contact parts
Ask the patient to remove glasses or contact lenses
Explain the air puff and reassure to reduce blinking
Reposition and repeat NCT, encouraging steady fixation and minimal blinking
Recognise that widely inconsistent readings are unreliable
If still inconsistent, arrange referral for Goldmann applanation tonometry
Document the attempts and the action taken
follow_up: Goldmann tonometry for an accurate IOP if NCT remains unreliable
Flag to the doctor if pressures cannot be reliably obtained
patient_education: Reassure the patient and coach steady fixation to reduce blinking
Explain why an accurate pressure reading matters
Explain a contact method (Goldmann) may be used if needed

key_points: Confirms identity and explains the test
Asks the patient to remove glasses/contact lenses
Performs hand hygiene and wipes machine contact parts
Repositions and repeats NCT with better technique
Does not record a doubtful single value
Knows when to refer for Goldmann tonometry
Understands the need for an accurate IOP
Uses judgement rather than recording a doubtful number
Arranges Goldmann tonometry if NCT remains unreliable
Coaches the patient to reduce blinking
Flags to the doctor as needed
